summary: Meta and BlackRock (with GIP and HPS) announced a joint venture, financed partly through a $12.5 billion debt facility, to develop a 1-gigawatt, roughly $14 billion data center campus in El Paso, Texas that Meta will lease as sole occupant to support its AI infrastructure.

mechanisms.reason: The campus is explicitly sized at 1 gigawatt of compute capacity dedicated to AI workloads.
mechanisms.quote: will have 1 gigawatt of compute capacity and will play an essential role in bringing Meta’s AI technologies to life

mechanisms.reason: The document discloses a specific, large capital commitment to build the data center campus.
mechanisms.quote: The parties have committed to fund their respective pro rata share of the approximately $14 billion in total development costs for the buildings and long-lived power, cooling, and connectivity infrastructure at the campus.

mechanisms.reason: Meta is using an external capital partner and debt financing rather than its own balance sheet to fund the buildout, changing how it accesses capital for compute expansion.
mechanisms.quote: A portion of BlackRock’s investment will be funded with proceeds from a $12.5 billion debt financing.

notable_reason: Discloses a large ($14B, 1GW) named data center financing structure with BlackRock, GIP and HPS, providing concrete figures on how Meta is funding AI compute expansion outside its own balance sheet.
